verses.text: “If you’re coming back, Israel,” says the LORD, “come back to me. Get those disgusting things out of my sight, and you won’t be driven away.
Then when you swear, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ you’ll mean it and do it with justice and integrity. The nations will find blessing in him and take pride in him.”
The LORD says to the people of Judah and Jerusalem, “Break up that hard ground you’ve left sitting, and quit planting seeds in the thorns.

People of Judah and Jerusalem, circumcise yourselves for the LORD. Cut away the foreskin of your hearts. Otherwise my anger will flare up over the evil you’ve done, and nobody will be able to put it out.
Spread the word across Judah and announce it in Jerusalem: ‘Sound the trumpet all over the land!’ Shout, ‘Everybody together! Let’s get inside the fortified cities!’
Raise a flag pointing to Zion. Run for safety! Don’t hang around. I’m bringing disaster out of the north, destruction on a huge scale.”
A lion has come out of his hiding place, a destroyer of nations. He’s on the move. He’s left his lair to wreck your land and leave your cities in ruins with nobody living there.
So put on sackcloth and cry out in grief. The LORD’s fierce anger still hasn’t let up on us.
“When that day comes,” says the LORD, “the king and the princes will lose their nerve. The priests will be stunned, and the prophets won’t know what to make of it.”
Then I said, “Oh, Lord GOD! You’ve really misled this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You’ll have peace,’ and now the sword is at our hearts.”
When that happens, this people and Jerusalem will hear, “A scorching wind is sweeping off the bare hills in the wilderness toward my people. It’s no breeze for sorting grain or cleaning it.
A wind full force from those hills will come at my bidding. Now I’ll pronounce my judgments against them.”
Look, he’s coming up like clouds rolling in. His chariots hit like a whirlwind, and his horses are faster than eagles. We’re in trouble! We’re wrecked.
Jerusalem, wash the evil out of your heart so you can be saved. How long are you going to let those evil thoughts live inside you?
A voice is calling from Dan, announcing disaster from the hills of Ephraim:
“Tell the nations. Put out this warning against Jerusalem: ‘Watchers are coming from a far country, shouting against the cities of Judah.
They’ve got Jerusalem surrounded like guards around a field, because she rebelled against me,’” says the LORD.
“The way you’ve lived and the things you’ve done brought this down on you. That’s your own evil coming back bitter enough to cut straight to your heart.”
It hurts! It hurts right in my heart! My heart is shaking inside me. How can I stay quiet? Deep inside, I’ve heard that trumpet, the alarm that means war.
One blow after another is decreed. The whole land is wrecked. Just like that, my tents are torn down and my curtains are gone in a flash.
How long will I keep seeing the battle flag and hearing that trumpet?
“My people are fools. They don’t know me. They’re clueless children who don’t understand a thing. They’re great at doing evil, but they have no idea how to do good.”
I looked at the earth. It was empty and ruined. I looked at the heavens. Their light was gone.
I looked at the mountains. They were shaking, and every hill was rocking back and forth.
I looked again. There wasn’t a person anywhere, and every bird in the sky had flown away.
I looked. The land that had grown so much was a wilderness, and all its cities lay broken in front of the LORD, under the heat of his anger.
The LORD says, “The whole land will lie in ruins, though I’ll stop short of wiping it all out.
That’s why the earth will grieve and the skies above will go black. I’ve said it and planned it. I haven’t changed my mind, and I won’t back down.”
At the sound of horsemen and archers, people run from every city. They duck into the brush and scramble up the rocks. Every city is abandoned. Nobody lives there.

And you, when you’re left in ruins, what will you do? Put on scarlet, cover yourself in gold jewelry, make your eyes look bigger with makeup. Dressing up gets you nowhere. Your lovers can’t stand you. They’re out to kill you.

I hear a cry like a woman in labor, the pain of someone giving birth for the first time. It’s Daughter Zion, gasping for air, reaching out her hands and saying, “I’m done for! I’m losing my strength right here in front of these killers.”
